items.front: Number-series detection ladder — what order do you test?
items.back: Difference → ratio → squares/cubes → prime gaps → alternating (two rules) → Fibonacci.

items.front: Consecutive odd differences (3,5,7,9) signal which pattern?
items.back: A square pattern, n² (or n²±k). E.g. 2,5,10,17,26 = n²+1.

items.front: How to crack an alternating (mixed) series?
items.back: Two operations applied turn by turn; test alternate gaps separately (e.g. /2 then ×3).

items.front: Wrong-term vs missing-term — the method for each?
items.back: Wrong: derive rule from the majority, flag the deviation. Missing: fix rule from neighbours, verify forward past the gap.
E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25 — count from the nearest anchor.
Opposite position = 27 − forward position. Pairs: A-Z, B-Y, C-X, D-W, M-N.

items.front: How to solve a grouped/combination alphabet series?
items.back: Split each block into columns and solve each column's own step; subtract 26 for wrap-around after Z.

items.front: Method for an alphanumeric series like C3, E5, G7, I9?
items.back: Track the letter pattern and the number pattern independently (letters +2; numbers odd → K11).

items.front: Letter-shift coding — the trap to watch for?
items.back: The shift can alternate (e.g. −1,+1). Verify sign on the sample; handle wrap-around (A−1=Z).

items.front: Rearrangement coding — how to identify the rule?
items.back: Same letters reordered — usually ascending alphabetical (BEHOLD→BDEHLO → COURSE→CEORSU).
Build a letter→digit map from the given word=code pair, keep letter order, then substitute for the target.
Intersect two sentences sharing a word to pin its code; the word common to all sentences takes the code common to all.
Do the base substitution first, THEN apply the overriding condition(s); watch for overlaps.
Find the relation in the first pair and apply it: n×(n+1) → 6×7=42, so 9×10=90.
CruX (C–X), LoVE (E–V), InneR (I–R), Jungle Queen (J–Q), KeeP (K–P), LOve (L–O); also A–Z, B–Y, D–W, M–N.

items.back: TMIGBA — the same letters sorted from Z down to A.

items.back: REGIT — reverse coding writes the word backwards.
